question: How many weeks of pregnancy make up a normal term delivery?
explanation: Great job! A normal, healthy pregnancy usually lasts between 37 and 42 weeks before natural labour begins. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: What is the main force that pushes the baby down during the first stage of labour?
explanation: You've got this! Uterine contractions do the heavy lifting to open the cervix and push the baby down even before the mother starts pushing. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: Why is it important for the baby to keep moving downward steadily during labour?

options.A: It allows all other cardinal movements to occur successfully
options.B: It stops maternal contractions from becoming too painful
options.C: It immediately closes the cervix after the baby passes
options.D: It prevents the placenta from detaching too early

explanation: Exactly! Continuous downward movement helps the baby's head touch the pelvic floor, triggering all the other cool turns and movements needed for birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: During the movement called flexion, what happens to the baby's chin?

options.A: It remains extended away from the body
options.B: It rotates fully toward the left hip
options.C: It points upward toward the maternal spine
options.D: It is pushed down to touch the chest

explanation: Correct! As the baby moves down, resistance from the pelvis makes the chin tuck neatly right against the chest. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: What is the big advantage when a baby's head is fully flexed?

options.A: It stops the fetus from turning into a breech position
options.B: It presents a smaller head diameter to the birth canal
options.C: It speeds up the dilation of the external cervical os
options.D: It prevents early rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Well done! Tucking the chin means the baby leads with a smaller part of the head, making it much easier to pass through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: Which muscle group helps guide the baby's head to rotate internally inside the pelvis?
explanation: You're doing great! The sloping levator ani muscles of the pelvic floor act like a slide, gently guiding the baby's head to turn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: During normal internal rotation, which way does the back of the baby's head (occiput) usually turn?

options.B: Toward the hollow of the sacrum
options.C: Toward the right lateral pelvic wall
options.D: Toward the left maternal iliac crest

explanation: Spot on! The occiput rotates forward toward the pubic bone so it can easily slip out of the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: As the baby's head extends to be born, which bone acts as the pivot point?
explanation: Correct! The baby's head pivots right under the mother's pubic bone, allowing it to lift upward and out into the world. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: During the extension movement, what part of the baby's face sweeps out of the vagina first?
explanation: You got it! As the head pivots up, the chin, mouth, and nose peek out first from under the perineum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What causes the movement called restitution right after the baby's head is born?

options.A: The shoulders push past the perineum simultaneously
options.B: The mother pushes extra hard to clear the airway
options.C: The midwife manually turns the baby to check for breathing
options.D: The head untwists to realign with the shoulders inside the pelvis

explanation: Brilliant! Restitution is just the head naturally untwisting and straightening out with the shoulders after it pops out. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: External rotation of the baby's head is actually caused by the turning of which body part?
explanation: Exactly! As the baby's shoulders twist inside to fit the pelvis, that movement travels up the neck and makes the head turn on the outside. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: During the final delivery of the baby's body, which part usually comes out first?
explanation: Spot on! The front shoulder slips out from under the pubic bone first, and then the back shoulder follows. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: Why does the rest of the baby's body slide out so quickly once the shoulders are born?

options.A: Maternal adrenaline production peaks right before delivery
options.B: The trunk and limbs are narrower than the head and shoulders
options.C: The amniotic fluid acts as a lubricant for the lower body
options.D: Uterine contractions become ten times stronger at this exact moment

explanation: You nailed it! Once the widest parts (head and shoulders) are safely out, the rest of the body is much narrower and slips right through. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)
